text:
Gabriel Landeskog won the Masterton last season for coming back from years of knee trouble, and this season he's simply playing. Ten points in 18 games at 14 to 15 minutes a night is a middle-six line, and Colorado has 56% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there.

His finishing is a touch hot (five goals on 4.4 expected), and his ice time has drifted down almost two minutes over the last ten games. Evolving-Hockey points out that he plays with very strong teammates (99th percentile), which flatters his on-ice numbers. Nobody in Denver is complaining: he's 33, he has a Calder and a Stanley Cup, and he's in the lineup every night.

He's still the captain in the way people notice. He went after Artyom Levshunov after a hit on Cale Makar, as Evan Rawal of the Denver Gazette wrote, and he fought Moritz Seider in Detroit. Our projection sees about 19 goals, which would be a fine number for a player people wondered would play again.
